 Profile Manage Profile Email Preferences Sign Out NBC Insider NBC100 A One Chicago Crossover Event Is Coming Soon in 2027! What We Know So Far
 Get the details on the latest mythic mash-up of One Chicago fan favorites in the 2027 crossover event.
 By Jessica White Nov 12, 2026, 12:09 PM ET Chicago's Finest Race to Stop Citywide Threat | One Chicago Crossover Event | NBC Now Playing 27:35 Web Exclusive Chicago's Finest Race to Stop Citywide Threat | One Chicago Crossover Event | NBC 4:38 Highlight Cops Clash With Violet & Novak During Paramedics Rescue | Chicago Fire 2:26 Highlight Mayday Called After Massive Warehouse Collapse | Chicago Fire Share this on Reddit Share this on Facebook Share this on X Share this by Email Share this by SMS Copy link Add us on Google Key Takeaways
 The next three-part One Chicago crossover event featuring Chicago Med , Chicago Fire , and Chicago P.D. premieres on NBC on Wednesday, January 13, 2027, starting at 8 p.m. ET.
 The storyline centers on a dramatic investigation into the death of a patient at Gaffney, with characters from all three series working together to uncover an unexpected suspect.
 All crossover episodes will stream the following day on Peacock
 The Windy City's favorite first responders are joining forces once again!
 How to Watch
 Watch Chicago Fire Wednesdays at 9 p.m. ET on NBC and next day on Peacock.
 Stream Now on Mark your calendars and set your alarms, because the casts of Chicago Med ,  Chicago Fire , and Chicago P.D . are getting together for another action-packed One Chicago crossover event. 
 While celebrating Chicago Fire 's 300th episode , Firehouse 51 icon Taylor Kinney opened up about the crossover event during his November 11 appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon . Kinney was eager to reveal that the next three-parter was coming in January 2027, relishing over the crossover episodes always being "a blast to produce."
 RELATED: A Guide to Every Must-Watch One Chicago Crossover Episode 
 Learn everything you need to know about the 2027 One Chicago crossover event, below.
 Officer Adam Ruzek (Patrick John Flueger) and Desk Sgt. Trudy Platt (Amy Morton) appear in Chicago Fire Season 13 Episode 11 "In The Trenches: Part 1". Photo: Peter Gordon/NBC When does the 2027 One Chicago crossover event premiere?
 The three-part One Chicago crossover airs on Wednesday, January 13, 2027, beginning at 8 p.m. ET on NBC.
 What to expect from the 2027 One Chicago crossover
 While an official trailer for One Chicago's three-part crossover hasn't hit yet, we've got some details about what to expect. Over the course of three episodes, an unexpected suspect related to the death of a patient at Gaffney will be the focus of a dramatic investigation that involves characters from P.D. , Med , and Fire. 
 RELATED: This Dramatic One Chicago Crossover Moment Took “Hours” to Put Together (EXCLUSIVE) 
 2027 will mark the third consecutive season in which the One Chicago characters have come together for a crossover event . While there have been dozens of One Chicago crossover pop-ins — a quick visit to Gaffney here, a pop-in from a detective there — it's always an action-packed affair anytime the heroes all team up.

 Where you can watch and stream the One Chicago crossover event
 Dr. Dean Archer (Steven Weber) appears on Chicago P.D. Season 12 Episode 14 "In The Trenches: Part III". Photo: Lori Allen/NBC All three episodes will be available to stream the next day on Peacock , the perfect place to binge all your favorite Med, Fire , and P.D. moments.
 While chatting about the 2026 crossover, Chicago Fire showrunner Andrea Newman opened up about the incredible lengths the producers go to to bring these epic team-ups to life.
 "It’s insanity, and it's a season-long process," Newman explained . "It really is. It starts pretty much from the jump, when we start talking about the possibilities. And these writers did incredible work together, but we all end up in there all the time. It's really an incredible feat to pull off. It is impossible the amount of people that are managed..."
 Newman continued, "Everybody goes all out. I will say everybody's just full pedal to the metal for these things. And, we end up at the end of it just being in awe of the crews and the cast that we have and the way they all come together... It's a lot of time, and a lot of work, and it's a lot of fun too."
